title: Oklahoma 56, Texas Tech 25 on November 22, 2003
question: What happened when No. 1 Oklahoma played Texas Tech on November 22, 2003?
answer: On November 22, 2003, top-ranked Oklahoma beat Texas Tech 56-25 in Lubbock. Jason White threw for 394 yards and four touchdowns, and Kejuan Jones scored five times, with the Sooners' defense intercepting B.J. Symons five times.
summary: On this date in 2003, No. 1 Oklahoma beat Texas Tech 56-25 in Lubbock as Jason White threw for 394 yards and Kejuan Jones scored five touchdowns.
body: Today is a good day to look back at a windy Saturday in Lubbock. On November 22, 2003, the top-ranked Sooners visited Texas Tech in a matchup billed as the nation's top offense against the nation's stingiest defense. Oklahoma arrived 11-0 and left 12-0, winning 56-25 before a crowd of 53,135.

Tech struck first with a field goal, but quarterback Jason White answered with touchdown passes to Travis Wilson and Mark Clayton for a 14-3 lead. Tech's B.J. Symons, who passed Ty Detmer's Division I single-season passing-yardage mark in the second quarter, pulled the Red Raiders within 14-10. Then Oklahoma took over, scoring three touchdowns in the last few minutes before halftime, two of them right after Symons interceptions, to lead 35-10 at the half.

White finished with 394 passing yards and four touchdowns, while running back Kejuan Jones scored five times: four short rushing touchdowns, from one or two yards out, and a 77-yard catch from White late in the fourth quarter. Oklahoma's defense picked off Symons five times, and he finished with 230 passing yards, well under his usual output.
The win was Oklahoma's 13th in a row and finished a 12-0 regular season. It also gave the Sooners a spot in the Big 12 title game in Kansas City on December 6, where they would meet Kansas State.
